paragraphs: The R500 uses the M113 — a 5.0-litre naturally aspirated V8 petrol engine that was a mainstay of Mercedes' V8 range during the 2000s. Fitted to the W251/V251 generation from 2006 until the R-Class was discontinued in 2013, it delivers the kind of effortless V8 performance that suits the R-Class's unique blend of MPV practicality and luxury car refinement. It's a robust, proven powerplant that responds well to a thorough rebuild when wear sets in.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every R500 on the road.

cards.body: A 5.0-litre V8 petrol engine fitted to the R500 from 2006 to 2013 (W251/V251 generation). It's a proven, durable V8 design shared across multiple Mercedes models of the era. We replace timing chains, bearings and gaskets as standard on every rebuild.

compatibility.intro: The R500 uses a single engine family — the M113 V8 — across its entire production run. However, there are still important compatibility checks to make: the exact year, drivetrain specification (4MATIC vs rear-wheel drive), and any running changes made during the 2006-2013 production run can affect which parts are correct for your car. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic R-Class quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
